correctness.rationale: Conditioning on a fixed vertex being isolated leaves the uniform m-edge graph on n-1 vertices. A copy cannot include the isolated vertex because H has no isolated vertices. Hence E[I X_H]=E[I] E_{n-1,m}[X_H]. Dividing the conditional and unconditional copy means gives (n-k)/n times (N)_e/(B)_e; subtracting one gives the displayed bracket, whose sign (not magnitude) is independent of m when both means are positive. Below e or above B one count is identically zero. In G(n,p) only the copy-placement ratio (n-k)/n remains because the edge presence probabilities cancel. Multiplying the fixed-edge brackets by n(B)_e gives the two stated opposite two-edge factors and the stated cubic for (k,e)=(5,3). The latter is negative at 6 and 7, increases for x>=8, and takes -30 at 10 and 64 at 11. An independently written standard-library replay, /workspace/branches/replay_5.py, checked exact moments for 837 graphs on five vertices (two motifs per graph) and 30,706 graphs on six vertices, and the three factorizations through n=200. The infinite claims use the analytic argument.
